Consorcio Shushufindi SA Files for Insolvency, Disrupting Ecuador’s Oil & Gas Sector

QUITO, Ecuador – Consorcio Shushufindi SA, one of Ecuador’s key players in the oil and gas production sector, has entered insolvency proceedings, triggering immediate operational disruptions and raising concerns across the industry.

The company, which operates several oilfields in the Sucumbíos province, announced on Monday that it had filed for insolvency, citing prolonged financial pressures amid fluctuating global oil prices and increased operational costs. As of Tuesday, company officials confirmed that production at some facilities has slowed significantly, while others are operating at minimal capacity.

“The decision to enter insolvency was not taken lightly,” said María Fernanda Hidalgo, spokesperson for Consorcio Shushufindi SA, in a prepared statement. “We are working closely with administrators to protect our employees and maintain essential operations as best as possible during this challenging period.”

The announcement has reverberated throughout Ecuador’s oil and gas sector, which remains a cornerstone of the national economy. According to figures from the Ecuadorian Petroleum Association, Consorcio Shushufindi SA was responsible for approximately seven percent of the country’s crude oil output in 2023.

Union representatives have voiced concern over the fate of the company’s workforce of more than 1,200 employees. “There is great uncertainty among the staff,” said Jorge Alarcón, leader of the Sucumbíos Oil Workers’ Union. “We urge the administrators to prioritize job security and provide clear communication during this process.”

Industry analysts say the insolvency could have wider implications for oil production targets and government revenues. “Given Shushufindi’s market share, a prolonged disruption may affect export volumes and fiscal projections,” said Gabriela Chávez, an energy sector analyst based in Quito.

While the immediate effects are being felt most acutely by the company and its employees, suppliers and local contractors are also bracing for delayed payments and contract renegotiations. The Ecuadorian Ministry of Energy said it is monitoring the situation closely but has not yet commented on potential interventions.

As insolvency proceedings continue, the future of Consorcio Shushufindi SA—and its impact on Ecuador’s crucial oil sector—remains uncertain.
